title: Chemical Cross-Linking to Study Protein Self-Assembly in Cellulo
author: Müller, Salman, et al.
materials: ECL Prime western blotting detection reagents

steps.title: Prepare and store all buffers
steps.instruction: Prepare the following solutions according to the Materials and Equipment list: HEPES Buffer, Tris Buffer, 0.5 % Glutaraldehyde Cross‑linking Solution, 4× LDS Sample Buffer, 1× MES Running Buffer, and Coomassie Stain (the stain may be stored separately). For recombinant protein work, also prepare a storage buffer consisting of 50 mM Tris‑HCl pH 7.5, 150 mM NaCl, 5 mM DTT, and 5 % glycerol. Store all buffers at the temperatures indicated in the key resources table; only the Coomassie Stain is excluded from the cross‑linking workflow. Maintain HEK293T cells in GlutaMAX medium supplemented with 10 % fetal bovine serum and 1 % penicillin/streptomycin at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Seed HEK293T cells for RNAi
steps.instruction: Seed HEK293T cells at 40–60 % confluence in 10 cm petri dishes so that each dish receives 2 × 10⁶ cells in a total volume of 10 mL pre‑warmed medium; use a Neubauer chamber to count cells and calculate the required volume. Prepare two dishes per experimental condition (one for siRNA, one for control scRNA). Incubate the dishes for 24 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ until they reach ~60–80 % confluence.

steps.title: Transfect cells with siRNA or control RNA
steps.instruction: For each condition, dilute 18 µL Lipofectamine RNAiMAX in 300 µL Opti‑MEM. Separately dilute 6 µL of 10 µM siRNA (or 6 µL of 10 µM control RNA) in 300 µL Opti‑MEM to obtain a final RNA amount of 30 pmol. Combine the diluted Lipofectamine with the diluted siRNA or scRNA in a 1:1 ratio and incubate 5 min at 20–22 °C to allow complex formation. Add the entire volume of the RNA‑lipid complex dropwise to the corresponding cell dish. Return the cells to the incubator and culture for 72 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Harvest and wash cells
steps.instruction: Scrape adherent cells from each dish with a cell scraper, collect the suspension in a 15 mL Falcon tube, and wash twice with ice‑cold PBS. For each wash, spin at 1500 rpm (435 × g) for 5 min at 4 °C using a Centrifuge 5810 R with rotor A‑4‑62, discard the supernatant without disturbing the pellet, and resuspend the pellet in 10 mL PBS before repeating the spin.

steps.title: Lyse cells in native buffer
steps.instruction: After the final PBS wash, remove as much residual PBS as possible without touching the pellet. Add 150 µL ice‑cold native lysis buffer to each pellet and gently resuspend by pipetting. To avoid clogging, trim the tip of a 1000 µL pipette tip by ~2 mm. Transfer the suspension to a fresh 1 mL Eppendorf tube.

steps.title: Sonicate lysates
steps.instruction: Sonicate the cell suspension in a Bioruptor Pico (Diagenode) at 60 % amplitude for 10 cycles of 30 s ON / 30 s OFF, keeping the samples at 4 °C. After sonication, centrifuge the lysates at 15 000 × g (Microcentrifuge 5425 with rotor FA‑45‑24‑11) for 20 min at 4 °C to pellet debris.

steps.title: Collect clarified lysate and quantify protein
steps.instruction: Carefully transfer the supernatant (clear lysate) to a clean 1 mL Eppendorf tube and keep on ice. Determine protein concentration using a method of choice (e.g., SDS‑PAGE with Coomassie staining of a defined sample volume such as 10 µL alongside a BSA standard curve). If lysates must be stored, freeze them only once in liquid nitrogen and thaw immediately before use; avoid repeated freeze‑thaw cycles as they reduce cross‑linking efficiency.
